chaucer-s-official-life: Scholar James Root Hulbert investigates the working life of Geoffrey Chaucer — not the poet of dreams, but the busy civil servant. As customs official, diplomat, and clerk of the king's works, Chaucer served the English crown for decades. Drawing on official records, Hulbert reconstructs the day-to-day career behind the Canterbury Tales.
little-citizens-the-humours-of-school-li: Myra Kelly taught on New York's Lower East Side, and these funny, tender stories draw on her immigrant pupils. Her little citizens — Irish, Jewish, and Italian children — navigate schoolroom English and American ways with irresistible wit. Behind the humor lies real affection, making the book both entertainment and a loving portrait of newcomers.
marguerite-verne-or-scenes-from-canadian: Rebecca Agatha Armour's novel paints scenes from Canadian life through the story of Marguerite Verne. One of the early works of Canadian fiction by a woman, it offers a valuable glimpse of the young Dominion's society. Pioneering, heartfelt, and historically precious.
how-to-live-a-holy-life: Charles Ebert Orr offers plain, practical guidance on Christian holiness for everyday believers — prayer, purity, and love woven into daily life. Simple, earnest, and devout, his counsel served generations of holiness-movement readers. A sincere and gentle manual of the spiritual life.
a-daughter-of-fife: Amelia Barr's Scottish heroine, a true daughter of Fife, faces love and hardship with sturdy courage and a warm heart. The author's gift for moral, heartfelt storytelling shines in this tale of the old country. A fine example of Barr's beloved historical fiction at its best.
venetian-life: William Dean Howells, fresh from his post as American consul, paints Venetian life — gondolas, palaces, cafés, and the quiet rhythm of the lagoons. His gentle, observant book charmed two nations and made his name. The classic American view of Venice.
gaut-gurley-or-the-trappers-of-umbagog-a: Daniel Pierce Thompson's frontier tale follows Gaut Gurley and the trappers of Umbagog through the Maine woods. Border warfare, Indian craft, and woodland skill fill these vigorous pages. A rousing early American novel of the northern frontier. Trap lines, border raids, and forest lore crowd this stirring tale of the northern woods.
septimius-felton-or-the-elixir-of-life: Hawthorne's Septimius Felton seeks the elixir of life — his unfinished romance of immortality and New England. Even incomplete, it fascinates. The master's last, lingering spell. Blood, flowers, and old manuscripts mingle in his eerie fragment. Hawthorne's shadow falls dark across this strange, sad fragment.
a-mummer-s-wife: George Moore's Mummer's Wife follows a strolling player's wife from respectability into drink and ruin. His unflinching French-style realism shocked Victorian England when it appeared. The novel helped remake English fiction for the modern age. A landmark, powerful and sad.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-flor: A 1913 entry on Floreffe, the White Canons' house in Belgium. Norbert's sons built it by the Sambre. Francis Martin Geudens writes its annals. Still a living house of prayer. Its mill and farms fed the canons for eight hundred years.
